newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ashton says sales up strongly in early 97.
newsitem.headline: Ashton says sales up strongly in early 97.

text.p: Diamond producer Ashton Mining Ltd said on Tuesday that its sales had picked up strongly in early 1997 after a slow start to direct marketing of its diamonds in the second half of calendar 1996.
Managing director John Robinson told the annual meeting Ashton also saw a brighter outlook for diamond demand in 1997.
"Sales picked up very strongly and we are making very good progress," he said.

In the middle of last year, Ashton withdrew from the Central Selling Organisation (CSO), a global diamond cartel run by South Africa's De Beers group, and set up its own direct marketing arm based in Antwerp. The CSO still controls about 75 percent of all trade in uncut diamonds.
Ashton has already said it expects sales revenue in calendar 1997 to exceed the A$181.5 million it reported in 1996, as the company beds down its new marketing arrangements.
RTZ-CRA owns the other 59.9 percent of the Argyle mine. Ashton itself is owned 46.95 percent by Malaysia Mining Corp.
Robinson on Tuesday painted a brighter picture of diamond demand from the world's major jewellery markets, especially Japan where demand slumped 14 percent in 1996.
"It's reasonable to expect Japan to start seeing some signs of improvement as the 1997 year develops," he told the meeting.
He also predicted further growth in the U.S. and Southeast Asian markets. "The outlook for 1997 is a good one," he said.

About 95 percent of Ashton's production is sold to the Indian diamond industry for cutting and polishing. In turn, the U.S., Japanese, Belgian and Hong Kong markets account for about 85 percent of Indian polished diamond exports, the company said.
